# orchestra_environment (Resource)

An Orchestra environment: a named set of values that pipeline runs resolve `${{ ENV.* }}` variables and integration credentials from.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "orchestra_environment" "production" {
  name        = "production"
  default_env = true

  # Values are always written as strings; `type` decides what is sent to the
  # API, so type = "int" with value = "8" sends the number 8.
  values = {
    WAREHOUSE = {
      type  = "string"
      value = "COMPUTE_WH"
    }
    BATCH_SIZE = {
      type  = "int"
      value = "500"
    }
    STRICT_MODE = {
      type  = "bool"
      value = "true"
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Environment name.
- `values` (Attributes Map) Environment values keyed by variable name. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--values))

### Optional

- `default_env` (Boolean) Whether this is the workspace's default environment. Leave unset to keep Orchestra's choice; it makes a workspace's first environment the default. Set `true` to promote this one. Only one environment can be the default; promoting one demotes the other outside Terraform's view.

### Read-Only

- `account_id` (String) Account the environment belongs to.
- `allow_unpublished_pipelines` (Boolean) Whether unpublished pipelines may run against this environment. Managed in the Orchestra UI.
- `allowed_branches` (List of String) Branches allowed to run against this environment. Managed in the Orchestra UI.
- `created_at` (String) When the environment was created.
- `id` (String) The environment ID.
- `updated_at` (String) When the environment was last updated.

<a id="nestedatt--values"></a>
### Nested Schema for `values`

Required:

- `type` (String) Value type.
- `value` (String) The value, always written as a string. It is converted to the type named above before being sent — `type = "int"` with `value = "3"` sends the number `3`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import orchestra_environment.production 9f8e7d6c-5b4a-3210-fedc-ba9876543210
```
